records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נִקְרָ֛א בְּסֵ֥פֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וְנִמְצָא֙ כָּת֣וּב בּ֔וֹ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־יָב֨וֹא עַמֹּנִ֧י וּמֹאָבִ֛י בִּקְהַ֥ל הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: On that day it was read in [the] book of Moses in [the] ears of the people, and was found written in it that not shall come an Ammonite and a Moabite into [the] assembly of God until forever,
pieces: On that day the book of Moses was read aloud for the people to hear, and in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,

L.1: On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people, and it was found written in it that an Ammonite or a Moabite shall not come into the assembly of God, even forever,

R.1: On that day the book of Moses was read aloud to the people. They found a law written in it that no one from Ammon or Moab could ever be a member of God's assembly,

decisions.choice: the law quoted: Deuteronomy 23:4-6
decisions.reason: The verse and the next sum up Deuteronomy 23:4-6 (Hebrew numbering; 23:3-5 in most Bibles): no Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD, "even to the tenth generation, forever", because they did not meet Israel with food and water and hired Balaam to curse them.

decisions.choice: the assembly of God: Israel gathered as God's people
decisions.reason: The assembly is the whole people gathered for worship and decision (Deuteronomy 23:2-9). To "enter" it means to be counted a full member of the worshiping community. The law in Deuteronomy does not bar every foreigner: Edomites and Egyptians could enter in the third generation (Deuteronomy 23:8-9).

decisions.choice: on that day: at a public reading of the law
decisions.reason: "On that day" links this reading loosely to the time of the dedication (12:43-44); it need not be the same day. Verses 4-6 show that the events of this chapter came after Nehemiah's return from the king, years after the wall was finished.

decisions.choice: read aloud for the people to hear (Balanced); read aloud to the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "in the ears of the people"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

records.heading: No Ammonite or Moabite in the assembly of God

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֧א קִדְּמ֛וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּלֶּ֣חֶם וּבַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֨ר עָלָ֤יו אֶת־בִּלְעָם֙ לְקַֽלְל֔וֹ וַיַּהֲפֹ֧ךְ אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ הַקְּלָלָ֖ה לִבְרָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: because not they met the sons of Israel with bread and with water, and he hired against him Balaam to curse him; and turned our God the curse into a blessing.
pieces: because they had not met the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} with food and water, but had hired Balaam against them to curse them; yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.

L.2: because they did not meet the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel with bread and with water, and [Moab] hired Balaam against him to curse him; and our God turned the curse into a blessing.

R.2: This was because the Ammonites and Moabites had not met the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} with food and water when they came out of Egypt. Instead, Moab paid Balaam to curse them. But our God turned that curse into a blessing.

decisions.choice: Balaam, and the curse turned to blessing
decisions.reason: Balak king of Moab hired the prophet Balaam to curse Israel, but God made him bless them instead (Numbers 22-24; Deuteronomy 23:5-6). "He hired" is singular in Hebrew: Moab, or its king, did the hiring.

decisions.choice: against him ... curse him: Israel as one people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of Israel as "him", one people, as Deuteronomy 23:5 does; the sense is the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: bread: food
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general, provisions for a people on the march (Deuteronomy 23:5; 2:28-29).

decisions.choice: when they came out of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable adds when this happened, from Deuteronomy 23:5.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "him"; Balanced and Readable use the plural that English uses for a people.

records.source: וַיְהִ֖י כְּשָׁמְעָ֣ם אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיַּבְדִּ֥ילוּ כָל־עֵ֖רֶב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was when they heard the law, and they separated all [the] mixed from Israel.
pieces: When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all who were of mixed descent.

L.3: And it happened, when they heard the law, that they separated all [the] mixed [people] from Israel.

R.3: When the people heard this law, they removed from Israel everyone who had foreign ancestors.

decisions.choice: the mixed: people of foreign descent
decisions.reason: The word is used of the "mixed crowd" of other peoples who left Egypt with Israel (Exodus 12:38). Here it means those of foreign, especially Ammonite and Moabite, descent living among Israel.

decisions.choice: separated from Israel: excluded from the assembly
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether they were sent away or only kept from the assembly and its worship; the law read in verse 1 concerns entering the assembly. The same separation is described in 9:2 and 10:29.

decisions.choice: the law: the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law here is what was read from the book of Moses in verse 1.

records.source: וְלִפְנֵ֣י מִזֶּ֔ה אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נָת֖וּן בְּלִשְׁכַּ֣ת בֵּית־אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ קָר֖וֹב לְטוֹבִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And before this, Eliashib the priest, appointed over [the] chamber of [the] house of our God, [was] related to Tobiah,
pieces: Before this, Eliashib the priest, who had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God and was related to Tobiah,

L.4: And before this, Eliashib the priest, appointed over the chamber of the house of our God, [was] related to Tobiah,

R.4: Earlier, Eliashib the priest had been put in charge of the storerooms in the temple of our God. Eliashib was related to Tobiah.

decisions.choice: Eliashib the priest: perhaps the high priest
decisions.reason: An Eliashib was high priest in Nehemiah's day (3:1; 12:10; 13:28). This Eliashib is called only "the priest" and has charge of the storerooms, so some think he is another man; but the high priest would have had authority over the temple rooms.

decisions.choice: Tobiah: Nehemiah's old opponent
decisions.reason: Tobiah the Ammonite official had opposed the rebuilding of the wall (2:10, 19; 4:1; 6:1-19). He had family ties with leading men of Judah (6:17-18). That an Ammonite should have a room in the temple courts runs directly against the law just read (verse 1).

decisions.choice: near to: related to
decisions.reason: The word means "near", here near by kinship or marriage (6:18 says Tobiah's son married into a Jerusalem family). It could also mean closely allied.

decisions.choice: the storerooms (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular "chamber", used for the storerooms as a group; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֜וֹ לִשְׁכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֗ה וְשָׁ֣ם הָי֪וּ לְפָנִ֟ים נֹ֠תְנִים אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֨ה הַלְּבוֹנָ֜ה וְהַכֵּלִ֗ים וּמַעְשַׂ֤ר הַדָּגָן֙ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר מִצְוַת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֑ים וּתְרוּמַ֖ת הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃
records.gloss: and he made for him a great chamber, and there they were formerly putting the grain offering, the frankincense, and the vessels, and [the] tithe of the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, [the] commandment of the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers, and the contribution of the priests.
pieces: had made a large chamber for him, where formerly they had put the grain offering, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and olive oil commanded for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.

L.5: and he made for him a great chamber, and there formerly they had been putting the grain offering, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, the commandment of the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers, and the contribution of the priests.

R.5: He gave Tobiah a large room that had been used to store the grain offerings, the incense, and the temple utensils. It had also held the tenth of the grain, new wine, and olive oil that God had commanded to be given to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the gifts that belonged to the priests.

decisions.choice: what the room had held
decisions.reason: The great storeroom held the gifts the people had pledged to bring (10:36-40) and that men were appointed to gather (12:44): offerings for the altar, the temple vessels, and the tithes and contributions that fed the priests, Levites, singers and gatekeepers. Clearing it for Tobiah meant those gifts had nowhere to go.

decisions.choice: the commandment of the Levites: what was commanded for them
decisions.reason: The phrase means the share commanded by law for the Levites, singers and gatekeepers (Numbers 18:21-24).

decisions.choice: new wine, fresh oil
decisions.reason: The words name the fresh produce of the vineyard and the olive grove, the usual pair in lists of tithes (Deuteronomy 14:23).

decisions.choice: incense
decisions.reason: Frankincense was a fragrant resin burned as incense (Leviticus 2:1-2); Readable uses the more common word.

records.source: וּבְכָל־זֶ֕ה לֹ֥א הָיִ֖יתִי בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֡י בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֜יִם לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֤סְתְּא מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ בָּ֣אתִי אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְקֵ֥ץ יָמִ֖ים נִשְׁאַ֥לְתִּי מִן־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And in all this not I was in Jerusalem, for in [the] year thirty and two of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I came to the king; and at [the] end of days I asked leave from the king,
pieces: While all this was happening I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. After some time I asked the king for leave

L.6: And in all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I came to the king; and at [the] end of days I asked leave from the king,

R.6: All this happened while I was away from Jerusalem. In the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes was king of Babylon, I had gone back to the king. After some time I asked him to let me go,

decisions.choice: the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes: 433 BC
decisions.reason: Nehemiah came to Jerusalem in Artaxerxes' twentieth year (2:1) and governed twelve years, until the thirty-second (5:14), which is about 433 BC. He then went back to the Persian court. Artaxerxes is called "king of Babylon" because Babylon was part of his empire, as Cyrus is in Ezra 5:13.

decisions.choice: at the end of days: after some time
decisions.reason: The phrase means after a period of time, not a stated length; it may have been a year or more. Nehemiah then came back to Jerusalem for a second term.

decisions.choice: I asked leave: I asked permission to go
decisions.reason: The verb "ask" in this form means to ask for oneself, here to ask the king's leave to return (compare 1 Samuel 20:6, 28).

records.source: וָאָב֖וֹא לִֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וָאָבִ֣ינָה בָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ לְט֣וֹבִיָּ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לוֹ֙ נִשְׁכָּ֔ה בְּחַצְרֵ֖י בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood about the evil that had done Eliashib for Tobiah, to make for him a chamber in [the] courts of [the] house of God.
pieces: and came to Jerusalem. Then I learned of the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah by giving him a room in the courts of the house of God.

L.7: and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in making a chamber for him in the courts of the house of God.

R.7: and came back to Jerusalem. There I found out about the evil thing Eliashib had done. He had given Tobiah a room in the courtyards of God's temple.

decisions.choice: the courts of the house of God
decisions.reason: The temple was surrounded by courtyards with rooms built around them, used for storage and for the priests (Ezekiel 40:17; 1 Chronicles 28:12). To give one to Tobiah, an Ammonite, was to bring into the holy place a man the law kept out of the assembly (verse 1).

decisions.choice: evil: a wrong, an outrage
decisions.reason: The word covers both moral wrong and harm. Nehemiah calls Eliashib's act a wrong because it broke the law and robbed the Levites of their storeroom (verses 5, 10).

decisions.choice: God's temple
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for "the house of God".

records.source: וַיֵּ֥רַֽע לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד וָֽאַשְׁלִ֜יכָה אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֧י בֵית־טוֹבִיָּ֛ה הַח֖וּץ מִן־הַלִּשְׁכָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was evil to me very much, and I threw all [the] vessels of [the] house of Tobiah outside from the chamber.
pieces: I was very displeased, and I threw all of Tobiah's household goods out of the room.

L.8: And it was very evil to me, and I threw all the vessels of the house of Tobiah outside, out of the chamber.

R.8: I was very angry. I threw all of Tobiah's furniture and belongings out of the room.

decisions.choice: it was evil to me: I was greatly displeased
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same word as verse 7: the wrong done was a wrong in Nehemiah's eyes too, and it angered him (compare 2:10, where the same idiom describes Tobiah's displeasure).

decisions.choice: the vessels of the house of Tobiah: his household goods
decisions.reason: "Vessels" means any articles or furnishings; with "house" it means the furniture and belongings Tobiah kept in the room.

decisions.choice: very angry
decisions.reason: Readable says the feeling in plain words.

records.source: וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה וַֽיְטַהֲר֖וּ הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת וָאָשִׁ֣יבָה שָּׁ֗ם כְּלֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְהַלְּבוֹנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I said, and they purified the chambers, and I brought back there [the] vessels of [the] house of God, the grain offering and the frankincense.
pieces: Then I gave orders, and they purified the rooms. I brought back into them the utensils of the house of God, with the grain offerings and the frankincense.

L.9: And I said, and they purified the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, the grain offering and the frankincense.

R.9: Then I gave orders for the rooms to be made ritually clean. After that I put the temple utensils back in them, with the grain offerings and the incense.

decisions.choice: they purified the chambers
decisions.reason: The rooms were made ritually clean after the use Tobiah had made of them, before the holy things were brought back. Nehemiah speaks of "chambers", plural: more rooms than the one large room may have been affected.

decisions.choice: I said: I gave orders
decisions.reason: "Said" is often used for a command given by a person in authority (Esther 1:10; Nehemiah 13:19, 22).

decisions.choice: incense
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: וָאֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּֽי־מְנָי֥וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לֹ֣א נִתָּ֑נָה וַיִּבְרְח֧וּ אִישׁ־לְשָׂדֵ֛הוּ הַלְוִיִּ֥ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים עֹשֵׂ֥י הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I knew that [the] portions of the Levites not had been given, and fled each to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work.
pieces: I also learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so that the Levites and the singers who did the work had fled, each to his own field.

L.10: And I knew that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and they had fled, each to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work.

R.10: I also found out that the Levites had not been given their share of the food. So the Levites and singers who served in the temple had left and gone back to work their own fields.

decisions.choice: each to his field: back to farming to live
decisions.reason: The Levites had no tribal land, only towns with pasture land around them (Numbers 35:2-5), and lived from the tithes (Numbers 18:21). With no tithes coming in, they had to farm to feed their families, and the temple's work was left undone.

decisions.choice: the portions not given: the pledge broken
decisions.reason: The people had pledged to bring the tithes to the Levites (10:38-40), and in Zerubbabel's and Nehemiah's days they had given them (12:47). Nehemiah now finds that this had stopped.

decisions.choice: doing the work: serving in the temple
decisions.reason: "The work" here is the service of the house of God (compare 11:12, 22).

records.source: וָאָרִ֨יבָה֙ אֶת־הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה מַדּ֖וּעַ נֶעֱזַ֣ב בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וָֽאֶ֨קְבְּצֵ֔םוָֽאַעֲמִדֵ֖ם עַל־עָמְדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I contended with the officials and I said: Why is forsaken [the] house of God? And I gathered them and I stationed them at their place.
pieces: So I contended with the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered the Levites and singers and set them at their posts.

L.11: And I contended with the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them and stationed them at their place.

R.11: So I took the officials to task. I asked them, "Why has God's temple been neglected?" Then I called the Levites and singers back and put them back at their posts.

decisions.choice: contended: brought a complaint against
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing a case or accusation against someone (also verses 17, 25). Nehemiah charges the leaders with failing in their duty.

decisions.choice: the house of God forsaken: the pledge of 10:40
decisions.reason: The people had ended their pledge with "we will not forsake the house of our God" (10:40); Nehemiah's question uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: them: the Levites and singers
decisions.reason: Those gathered and stationed are the Levites and singers who had left (verse 10), not the officials.

decisions.choice: the Levites and singers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "them" are, from verse 10.

records.source: וְכָל־יְהוּדָ֗ה הֵבִ֜יאוּ מַעְשַׂ֧ר הַדָּגָ֛ן וְהַתִּיר֥וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֖ר לָאוֹצָרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And all Judah brought [the] tithe of the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil to the storehouses.
pieces: Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, new wine, and olive oil into the storehouses.

L.12: And all Judah brought the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil into the storehouses.

R.12: Then all the people of Judah brought a tenth of their grain, new wine, and olive oil to the storerooms.

decisions.choice: all Judah brought the tithe
decisions.reason: The whole people of the province took up again what they had pledged (10:38-39); the stores that fed the temple servants were filled once more.

decisions.choice: a tenth of their grain
decisions.reason: Readable says what a tithe is.

records.source: וָאוֹצְרָ֣ה עַל־א֠וֹצָרוֹת שֶׁלֶמְיָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְצָד֣וֹק הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וּפְדָיָה֙ מִן־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְעַל־יָדָ֔ם חָנָ֥ן בֶּן־זַכּ֖וּר בֶּן־מַתַּנְיָ֑ה כִּ֤י נֶאֱמָנִים֙ נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וַעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לַחֲלֹ֥ק לַאֲחֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And I made treasurers over [the] storehouses Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah from the Levites, and at their hand Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, for reliable they were counted, and on them [was] to distribute to their brothers.
pieces: And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, for they were counted reliable. Their duty was to distribute to their brothers.

L.13: And I made treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah from the Levites, and at their hand Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, for they were counted reliable, and on them [it was] to distribute to their brothers.

R.13: I put three men in charge of the storerooms: Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah, a Levite. Hanan son of Zaccur and grandson of Mattaniah was their helper. Everyone knew these men could be trusted. Their job was to hand out the supplies fairly to the other priests and Levites.

decisions.choice: a priest, a scribe and a Levite
decisions.reason: Nehemiah set a mixed board over the stores, a priest, a scribe and a Levite, with an assistant from the singers' family of Mattaniah (12:8, 35), so that no one group, and no single man like Eliashib (verse 4), held the stores alone.

decisions.choice: counted reliable: known to be trustworthy
decisions.reason: The word means faithful, dependable; it is the quality Nehemiah looked for in Hananiah (7:2). It describes the men's character, not an office.

decisions.choice: at their hand: as their assistant
decisions.reason: "At the hand of" someone means beside him as a helper (3:2-12, where the same phrase is "next to him"; 1 Chronicles 25:2-3).

decisions.choice: fairly to the other priests and Levites
decisions.reason: Readable says who "their brothers" were and what was handed out; "fairly" is implied by the stress on the men's trustworthiness.

records.source: זָכְרָה־לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י עַל־זֹ֑את וְאַל־תֶּ֣מַח חֲסָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהַ֖י וּבְמִשְׁמָרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Remember for me, my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my loyal deeds that I have done in [the] house of my God and in its services.
pieces: Remember me, my God, for this, and do not wipe out the faithful deeds I have done for the house of my God and for its services.

L.14: Remember for me, my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my deeds of steadfast love that I have done in the house of my God and in its services.

R.14: My God, remember me for this. Do not forget the faithful things I have done for the temple of my God and for the work done there.

decisions.choice: Remember me, my God: Nehemiah's prayer for God's favor
decisions.reason: Nehemiah breaks into his account with short prayers asking God to remember his work for good (5:19; 13:22, 31) and to remember his enemies for what they did (6:14; 13:29). To "remember" in such prayers is not only to recall but to act on what is remembered, to reward or to judge (Genesis 8:1; Psalm 25:7).

decisions.choice: my loyal deeds: acts of faithful love
decisions.reason: The word usually names God's steadfast love (verse 22). Used of a person, it means deeds of loyalty and devotion, here Nehemiah's care for the temple and its servants (2 Chronicles 32:32; 35:26 use it of the good deeds of Hezekiah and Josiah).

decisions.choice: do not wipe out: do not erase from your record
decisions.reason: The picture is of a written record from which a name or deed can be wiped (Exodus 32:32-33; Psalm 69:29). Nehemiah asks that his faithful work stay written before God.

decisions.choice: its services: the duties of the temple
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "charge" in 12:45: the set duties of the priests, Levites, singers and gatekeepers that Nehemiah had restored.

decisions.choice: Remember for me, my God (Literal); Remember me, my God (Balanced); My God, remember me (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of Nehemiah's prayer is kept the same wherever it comes (5:19; 13:22, 31). Literal keeps the Hebrew "for me" (to my credit).

decisions.choice: faithful deeds; faithful things
decisions.reason: "Faithful" carries the project's word for this term (faithful love) into a phrase that suits human acts; Literal keeps "steadfast love". Readable says "do not forget" for "do not wipe out".

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה רָאִ֣יתִי בִֽיהוּדָ֣ה׀דֹּֽרְכִֽים־גִּתּ֣וֹת׀בַּשַּׁבָּ֡ת וּמְבִיאִ֣ים הָעֲרֵמ֣וֹת וְֽעֹמְסִ֪ים עַל־הַחֲמֹרִ֟ים וְאַף־יַ֜יִן עֲנָבִ֤ים וּתְאֵנִים֙ וְכָל־מַשָּׂ֔א וּמְבִיאִ֥ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וָאָעִ֕יד בְּי֖וֹם מִכְרָ֥ם צָֽיִד׃
records.gloss: In the days the those I saw in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing the heaps and loading on the donkeys, and also wine, grapes and figs and every load, and bringing [them to] Jerusalem on [the] day of the Sabbath; and I warned on [the] day of their selling food.
pieces: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, figs, and every kind of load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. I warned them on the day they sold food.

L.15: In those days I saw in Judah [people] treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps [of grain] and loading [them] on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs and every [kind of] load, and bringing [them into] Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; and I warned [them] on the day they sold food.

R.15: At that time I saw people in Judah working on the Sabbath. Some were pressing grapes to make wine. Others were bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of other goods, to carry into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. I warned them not to sell food on that day.

decisions.choice: work on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law forbade work on the seventh day, the Sabbath (Exodus 20:8-11; Deuteronomy 5:12-15), and the people had pledged not to buy goods or grain from the peoples of the land on that day (10:32). Treading grapes, carrying loads and selling were all work.

decisions.choice: carrying loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had warned Jerusalem: "do not carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem" (Jeremiah 17:21-27). Nehemiah's words in verses 18-19 echo that warning.

decisions.choice: I warned them on the day they sold food
alternatives: I warned them against selling food on that day
decisions.reason: The words can mean that Nehemiah warned them on the very day they were selling, or that he warned them about selling food on that day. Either way the warning was against Sabbath trade.

decisions.choice: heaps: heaps of grain
decisions.reason: The word is used of heaps of harvested grain (Ruth 3:7; 2 Chronicles 31:6-9).

decisions.choice: pressing grapes to make wine
decisions.reason: Readable says what treading a winepress was, and follows the alternative reading of the warning, marked uncertain in the meaning decision.

records.source: וְהַצֹּרִים֙ יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ מְבִיאִ֥ים דָּ֖אג וְכָל־מֶ֑כֶר וּמֹכְרִ֧ים בַּשַּׁבָּ֛ת לִבְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And the Tyrians lived in it, bringing fish and every [kind of] merchandise and selling on the Sabbath to [the] sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
pieces: Men of Tyre who lived there were bringing in fish and all kinds of goods and selling them on the Sabbath to the {{gender:people|sons}} of Judah, in Jerusalem itself.

L.16: And Tyrians lived in it, bringing in fish and every [kind of] merchandise and selling [them] on the Sabbath to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah, and in Jerusalem.

R.16: Some men from the city of Tyre were living in Jerusalem. They brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them to the people of Judah on the Sabbath, right there in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Tyrians: traders from Tyre
decisions.reason: Tyre on the Phoenician coast was a city of traders (Ezekiel 27); it had long sold timber and goods to Jerusalem (1 Kings 5; Ezra 3:7). These merchants, living in the city, were not bound by the Sabbath, but the people of Judah who bought from them were.

decisions.choice: in it ... and in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "In it" refers to Jerusalem, or perhaps to Judah. The last words, "and in Jerusalem", stress that the Sabbath was being broken in the holy city itself.

decisions.choice: children of Judah (Literal); people of Judah (Balanced), with the gender setting
decisions.reason: "Sons of Judah" means the people of Judah, men and women; the traditional wording is the setting's alternative.

records.source: וָאָרִ֕יבָה אֵ֖ת חֹרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם מָֽה־הַדָּבָ֨ר הָרָ֤ע הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים וּֽמְחַלְּלִ֖ים אֶת־י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃
records.gloss: And I contended with [the] nobles of Judah and I said to them: What [is] the thing, the evil, the this, which you [are] doing, and profaning the day of the Sabbath?
pieces: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?

L.17: And I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What [is] this evil thing which you are doing, and profaning the Sabbath day?

R.17: So I took the leaders of Judah to task. I said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing? You are treating the Sabbath as if it were not holy!

decisions.choice: profaning the Sabbath: treating the holy day as common
decisions.reason: To profane is to treat what is holy as ordinary. The Sabbath was holy to the LORD (Exodus 31:14-16; Ezekiel 20:13); using it for trade made it a common day.

decisions.choice: the nobles of Judah: the leading families
decisions.reason: Nehemiah holds the leading men responsible, as in 5:7, since they had the power to stop the trade and had signed the pledge (10:32).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: The project's Readable word for the nobles (2:16).

records.source: הֲל֨וֹא כֹ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ אֲבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַיָּבֵ֨א אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ עָלֵ֗ינוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְעַ֖ל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְאַתֶּ֞ם מוֹסִיפִ֤ים חָרוֹן֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְחַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃פ
records.gloss: Not thus did your fathers do, and brought our God on us all the evil, the this, and on the city, the this? And you [are] adding wrath on Israel to profane the Sabbath.
pieces: Did not your ancestors do the same, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? Yet you are adding to the wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."

L.18: Did not your fathers do thus, and our God brought on us all this evil, and on this city? And you are adding wrath on Israel to profane the Sabbath."

R.18: Your ancestors did the same thing, and that is why our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city! Now you are making God even more angry with Israel by treating the Sabbath as if it were not holy."

decisions.choice: the fathers' Sabbath-breaking and the city's ruin
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had warned that if Jerusalem kept carrying loads in on the Sabbath, God would set fire to its gates and its palaces (Jeremiah 17:27). The city was burned by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:9). Nehemiah reads that disaster as the punishment Jeremiah announced.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster
decisions.reason: The same word as "evil" in verse 17; here it is the evil that came on the people, disaster or harm. The play on the word is in the Hebrew: their evil deed brings evil on them.

decisions.choice: adding wrath: bringing more of God's anger
decisions.reason: The anger is God's (Ezra 10:14). Nehemiah warns that breaking the Sabbath again adds to the judgment already suffered.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the earlier generations, men and women; Literal keeps "fathers".

records.source: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צָֽלֲלוּ֩ שַׁעֲרֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לִפְנֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת וָאֹֽמְרָה֙ וַיִּסָּגְר֣וּ הַדְּלָת֔וֹת וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִפְתָּח֔וּם עַ֖ד אַחַ֣ר הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וּמִנְּעָרַ֗י הֶֽעֱמַ֨דְתִּי֙ עַל־הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לֹא־יָב֥וֹא מַשָּׂ֖א בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃
records.gloss: And it was, when grew shady [the] gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, and I said, and were shut the doors, and I said that not they should open them until after the Sabbath; and [some] of my young men I stationed at the gates, [that] not a load should come in on [the] day of the Sabbath.
pieces: When the shadows fell on the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and gave orders that they were not to be opened until after the Sabbath. I stationed some of my own men at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.

L.19: And it happened, when the gates of Jerusalem grew dark before the Sabbath, that I gave orders, and the doors were shut; and I said that they should not open them until after the Sabbath. And I stationed [some] of my young men at the gates, [so that] no load should come in on the Sabbath day.

R.19: On Friday evening, as it began to get dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered that the city gates be shut and kept shut until the Sabbath was over. I put some of my own men at the gates to make sure no goods were brought in on the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: as the gates grew dark: the Sabbath began at sunset
decisions.reason: The day was counted from evening to evening (Leviticus 23:32), so the Sabbath began at sunset on the sixth day. Nehemiah had the gates shut as the shadows fell, before the Sabbath began.

decisions.choice: my young men: Nehemiah's own attendants
decisions.reason: The word means young men, servants or attendants. Nehemiah's men had worked and stood guard with him on the wall (4:10, 17; 5:10, 16).

decisions.choice: On Friday evening
decisions.reason: Readable names the day for a modern reader: the evening before the Sabbath, which falls on Saturday. The Hebrew says only "before the Sabbath".

records.heading: Keeping the Sabbath holy

records.source: וַיָּלִ֨ינוּ הָרֹכְלִ֜ים וּמֹכְרֵ֧י כָל־מִמְכָּ֛ר מִח֥וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִָ֖ם פַּ֥עַם וּשְׁתָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And spent the night the traders and sellers of every [kind of] merchandise outside Jerusalem once and twice.
pieces: Once or twice the traders and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.

L.20: And the traders and sellers of every [kind of] merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem once or twice.

R.20: Once or twice the merchants and people selling all kinds of goods camped for the night outside Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: waiting outside the walls
decisions.reason: With the gates shut, the traders camped outside the walls, ready to sell when the gates opened, or to sell outside to people who came out to them.

records.source: וָאָעִ֣ידָה בָהֶ֗ם וָאֹמְרָ֤ה אֲלֵיהֶם֙ מַדּ֜וּעַ אַתֶּ֤ם לֵנִים֙ נֶ֣גֶד הַחוֹמָ֔ה אִם־תִּשְׁנ֕וּ יָ֖ד אֶשְׁלַ֣ח בָּכֶ֑ם מִן־הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא לֹא־בָ֖אוּ בַּשַּׁבָּֽת׃ס
records.gloss: And I warned them and said to them: Why [are] you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do [it] again, a hand I will send on you. From the time, that, not they came on the Sabbath.
pieces: But I warned them, "Why are you spending the night by the wall? If you do it again, I will use force against you." From then on they did not come on the Sabbath.

L.21: And I warned them and said to them, "Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do [it] again, I will lay a hand on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.

R.21: But I warned them. I said, "Why are you camping by the wall? If you do this again, I will have you arrested." From then on they stopped coming on the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: send a hand on you: use force against you
decisions.reason: To "send a hand" against someone is to take hold of them, to arrest or attack them (Genesis 22:12; Esther 2:21).

decisions.choice: warned: solemnly testified against
decisions.reason: The verb means to warn as a witness does, giving formal notice of what will follow (also verse 15; 9:29-30).

decisions.choice: have you arrested
decisions.reason: Readable gives one likely meaning of the threat; the Hebrew does not say what form the force would take.

records.source: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽהְי֤וּ מִֽטַּהֲרִים֙ וּבָאִים֙ שֹׁמְרִ֣ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת גַּם־זֹאת֙ זָכְרָה־לִּ֣י אֱלֹהַ֔י וְח֥וּסָה עָלַ֖י כְּרֹ֥ב חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃פ
records.gloss: And I said to the Levites that they should be purifying themselves and coming, guarding the gates, to keep holy the day of the Sabbath. Also this remember for me, my God, and have pity on me according to [the] greatness of your steadfast love.
pieces: Then I told the Levites to purify themselves and come and guard the gates, so as to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me, my God, for this also, and spare me according to the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love.

L.22: And I told the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. This also remember for me, my God, and have pity on me according to the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} steadfast love.

R.22: Then I told the Levites to make themselves ritually clean and to go and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. My God, remember me for this too. Have mercy on me, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love is so great.

decisions.choice: Levites as Sabbath guards
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's own men had kept the gates for a time (verse 19); now he hands the task to the Levites, who already kept the temple gates (12:25). Because keeping the Sabbath holy was a holy duty, they first purified themselves.

decisions.choice: have pity on me: spare me
decisions.reason: The verb means to look with pity and spare (Psalm 72:13; Joel 2:17). Nehemiah does not claim his deeds earn God's favor; he asks for it on the ground of God's great love.

decisions.choice: your steadfast love: God's faithful covenant love
decisions.reason: The word is God's loyal, covenant love, as in 1:5 and 9:17, 32.

decisions.choice: remember for me, my God (Literal); Remember me, my God (Balanced); My God, remember me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's prayer keeps the same wording each time it comes (13:14, 31).

decisions.choice: because your faithful love is so great
decisions.reason: Readable turns "according to the greatness of" into a plain reason clause.

records.source: גַּ֣ם׀בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־הַיְּהוּדִים֙ הֹשִׁ֗יבוּ נָשִׁים֙ אַשְׁדֳּדִיּ֔וֹתעַמֳּנִיּ֖וֹתמוֹאֲבִיּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Also in the days, those, I saw the Jews [who] had married women, Ashdodites, Ammonites, Moabites.
pieces: In those days I also saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

L.23: Also in those days I saw the Jews [who] had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, of Moab.

R.23: At that time I also saw that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

decisions.choice: Ashdod, Ammon, Moab: neighboring peoples
decisions.reason: Ashdod was one of the old Philistine cities on the coast, by then the center of a Persian province and among Nehemiah's opponents (4:1). Ammon and Moab lay east of the Jordan, the peoples named in the law read in verse 1.

decisions.choice: had married: literally "had caused to dwell"
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle a wife in one's house, a way of saying "to marry" used in Ezra 10:2, 10 for the same situation. The people had pledged not to make such marriages (10:31), as Ezra had dealt with a generation earlier (Ezra 9-10).

decisions.choice: the spelling of Ashdodites and Ammonites
decisions.reason: The written consonants of these two words differ slightly from the way the text is read, as the Masoretes noted in the margin (the qere). This translation follows the reading, as the source data does; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: some Jewish men
decisions.reason: Readable says "some" because the text does not mean that all the Jews had done this.

records.heading: Foreign wives and the covenant of the priesthood

records.source: וּבְנֵיהֶ֗ם חֲצִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אַשְׁדּוֹדִ֔ית וְאֵינָ֥ם מַכִּירִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוּדִ֑ית וְכִלְשׁ֖וֹן עַ֥ם וָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And their children, half [was] speaking Ashdodite, and not they [were] knowing [how] to speak Judean, and according to [the] language of people and people.
pieces: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, or the language of one people or another, and they did not know how to speak the language of Judah.

L.24: And their children, half spoke Ashdodite, and they did not know [how] to speak Judean, but [spoke] according to the language of people and people.

R.24: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of one of the other peoples. They could not speak the language of Judah.

decisions.choice: Judean: the Hebrew language
decisions.reason: "Judean" is the language of Judah, Hebrew, as in 2 Kings 18:26, 28 and Isaiah 36:11, 13, where it is set against Aramaic. The children of these marriages grew up unable to understand the language in which the law was read (8:1-8).

decisions.choice: the language of people and people: of one people or another
decisions.reason: The repeated noun means "of each people": the children spoke the language of whatever people their mother came from (compare Esther 1:22).

decisions.choice: Ashdodite: the language of Ashdod
decisions.reason: What language this was is not known; Philistine had probably died out, and it may have been a local dialect of Aramaic or of the coastal Canaanite languages.

decisions.choice: the order of the clauses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two kinds of foreign speech together and end with what the children could not speak; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: וָאָרִ֤יב עִמָּם֙ וָאֲקַֽלְלֵ֔ם וָאַכֶּ֥ה מֵהֶ֛ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וָֽאֶמְרְטֵ֑ם וָאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֣ם בֵּֽאלֹהִ֗ים אִם־תִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ לִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִם־תִּשְׂאוּ֙ מִבְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֖ם וְלָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I contended with them and I cursed them and I struck men of them and I pulled out their hair, and I made them swear by God: If you will give your daughters to their sons, and if you will take of their daughters for your sons and for yourselves!
pieces: And I contended with them and cursed them, and I struck some of their men and pulled out their hair. And I made them swear by God, "You will not give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves."

L.25: And I contended with them and cursed them, and I struck men of them and pulled out their hair, and I made them swear by God, "[May God judge you] if you give your daughters to their sons, and if you take of their daughters for your sons and for yourselves!"

R.25: I argued with them and called down curses on them. I beat some of the men and pulled out their hair. Then I made them take an oath in God's name: "You will not let your daughters marry their sons, and you will not take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves."

decisions.choice: If you give ...: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: A Hebrew oath often names the forbidden act with "if" and leaves the curse unsaid ("may God punish me if ...", compare 1 Samuel 3:17). "If you give" therefore means "you shall not give".

decisions.choice: not giving or taking daughters in marriage
decisions.reason: The words repeat the law (Deuteronomy 7:3) and the people's own pledge (10:31) almost exactly.

decisions.choice: cursed, struck, pulled out hair: public shaming and punishment
decisions.reason: Nehemiah acted as governor with authority to punish (compare Ezra 7:26). Pulling out the hair or beard was a public humiliation (2 Samuel 10:4; Isaiah 50:6). When Ezra faced the same sin, he pulled out his own hair in grief (Ezra 9:3).

decisions.choice: You will not ... (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Hebrew oath form into a plain promise. Literal keeps the "if" form and supplies the unsaid curse in brackets. Nehemiah's speech goes on into verses 26-27.

records.source: הֲל֣וֹא עַל־אֵ֣לֶּה חָטָֽא־שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וּבַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָרַבִּים֩ לֹֽא־הָיָ֨ה מֶ֜לֶךְ כָּמֹ֗הוּ וְאָה֤וּב לֵֽאלֹהָיו֙ הָיָ֔ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֣הוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־אוֹת֣וֹ הֶחֱטִ֔יאוּ הַנָּשִׁ֖ים הַנָּכְרִיּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Not on these did sin Solomon king of Israel? And among the nations, the many, not there was a king like him, and loved by his God he was, and made him God king over all Israel; also him caused to sin the women, the foreign.
pieces: "Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet even he was made to sin by foreign wives.

L.26: "Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on these [things]? And among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel; even him the foreign women caused to sin.

R.26: "Remember Solomon, king of Israel! Women like these led him into sin. There was no king like him in all the nations. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel. But even Solomon was led into sin by his foreign wives.

decisions.choice: Solomon and his foreign wives
decisions.reason: Solomon married many foreign women, Moabite, Ammonite and others, and in his old age they turned his heart to their gods (1 Kings 11:1-8). The law had warned that such marriages would lead Israel's sons to other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4).

decisions.choice: no king like him; loved by his God
decisions.reason: God promised Solomon wisdom and riches beyond any other king (1 Kings 3:12-13). At his birth the LORD loved him, and he was named Jedidiah, "loved by the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:24-25).

decisions.choice: on these: on account of such things
decisions.reason: "These" can mean these women or these deeds, marriages like these; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Remember Solomon ...!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the rhetorical question into a statement so the point is plain.

decisions.choice: foreign wives
decisions.reason: The project's wording for these foreign women in Ezra and Nehemiah; Literal keeps "women".

records.source: וְלָכֶ֣ם הֲנִשְׁמַ֗ע לַעֲשֹׂת֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את לִמְעֹ֖ל בֵּֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְהֹשִׁ֖יב נָשִׁ֥ים נָכְרִיּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And to you shall we listen to do all the evil, the great, the this, to act unfaithfully against our God by marrying women, foreign?
pieces: Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign wives?"

L.27: And shall we listen to you, to do all this great evil, to act unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?"

R.27: Should we just let you go on doing this terrible evil? You are being unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign wives!"

decisions.choice: shall we listen to you: two possible readings
alternatives: Must we hear about you doing all this great evil?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean "shall we then listen to you (and do the same)?" or "must it be heard of you that you do this?" Either way Nehemiah refuses to accept such marriages.

decisions.choice: act unfaithfully: break faith with God
decisions.reason: The verb means to break faith, to betray a trust; it is the word Ezra used for the same marriages (Ezra 9:2, 4; 10:2, 10).

decisions.choice: Should we just let you go on ...?
decisions.reason: Readable follows the sense common to both readings, that Nehemiah will not let it pass.

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵ֨י יוֹיָדָ֤ע בֶּן־אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל חָתָ֖ן לְסַנְבַלַּ֣ט הַחֹרֹנִ֑י וָאַבְרִיחֵ֖הוּ מֵעָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And [one] of [the] sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the priest, the great, [was] son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; and I drove him away from me.
pieces: And one of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; so I drove him away from me.

L.28: And one of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the great priest [was] son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; and I drove him away from me.

R.28: One of the grandsons of Eliashib the high priest, a son of Joiada, had married the daughter of Sanballat from Beth-horon. So I chased him away from me.

decisions.choice: Sanballat the Horonite
decisions.reason: Sanballat was the leader of the opposition to the rebuilding of the wall (2:10, 19; 3:33; 6:1-14). A letter from Elephantine in Egypt (407 BC) names Sanballat as governor of Samaria. "Horonite" probably means he came from Beth-horon, northwest of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a priest's family married to the enemy
decisions.reason: The high priest had to marry a woman of his own people (Leviticus 21:14), and the priests were to keep their line pure. A grandson of the high priest, perhaps in line to be high priest himself, had married the daughter of Israel's chief opponent.

decisions.choice: the high priest: Eliashib
decisions.reason: "The high priest" probably describes Eliashib (3:1), though Joiada, his son, may have succeeded him by this time (12:10, 22).

decisions.choice: drove him away from me: expelled him
decisions.reason: Nehemiah drove him out of his presence, and so out of the priestly service in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: had married the daughter of; from Beth-horon
decisions.reason: Readable explains "son-in-law" and "Horonite".

records.source: זָכְרָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהָ֑י עַ֚ל גָּאֳלֵ֣י הַכְּהֻנָּ֔ה וּבְרִ֥ית הַכְּהֻנָּ֖ה וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: Remember for them, my God, on [the] defilements of the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
pieces: Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.

L.29: Remember for them, my God, on [account of] the defilements of the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.

R.29: My God, remember what these people have done. They have made the priesthood unclean, and they have broken the covenant {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with the priests and the Levites.

decisions.choice: the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites
decisions.reason: God's covenant with Levi and with Phinehas gave the priests their office and asked them to be faithful (Numbers 25:12-13; Malachi 2:4-8). Malachi, in the same period, also charges the priests with corrupting the covenant of Levi.

decisions.choice: Remember them: remember against them
decisions.reason: This is Nehemiah's prayer for judgment, the reverse of his prayer for himself (verses 14, 22, 31), as in 6:14.

decisions.choice: defilements: what made the priesthood unclean
decisions.reason: The word means defilement or pollution (compare Ezra 2:62, where unproven priests were kept out "as unclean"). Marriages like the one in verse 28 defiled the priestly line.

decisions.choice: the covenant you made
decisions.reason: Readable says whose covenant it was.

records.source: וְטִֽהַרְתִּ֖ים מִכָּל־נֵכָ֑ר וָאַעֲמִ֧ידָה מִשְׁמָר֛וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ בִּמְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I purified them from all foreignness, and I established duties for the priests and for the Levites, each in his work,
pieces: So I purified them of everything foreign, and I set out the duties of the priests and the Levites, each in his own task,

L.30: And I purified them from everything foreign, and I established duties for the priests and for the Levites, each in his work,

R.30: So I made the priests and Levites clean from everything foreign. I gave each of the priests and Levites his own duties to carry out.

decisions.choice: purified them from everything foreign
decisions.reason: Nehemiah removed foreign influence from the priests and Levites, the foreign marriages above all (verses 23-29), and so made them fit to serve.

decisions.choice: duties: the courses of service
decisions.reason: The word means watches or set duties: the divisions in which the priests and Levites took turns to serve (12:9, 24; 1 Chronicles 24-26).

records.source: וּלְקֻרְבַּ֧ן הָעֵצִ֛ים בְּעִתִּ֥ים מְזֻמָּנ֖וֹת וְלַבִּכּוּרִ֑יםזָכְרָה־לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָֽה׃
records.gloss: and for [the] offering of the wood at times appointed, and for the firstfruits. Remember for me, my God, for good.
pieces: and I provided for the wood offering at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, my God, for good.

L.31: and for the offering of the wood at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember for me, my God, for good.

R.31: I also arranged for the wood for the altar to be brought at the right times, and for the first part of each harvest to be given. My God, remember me and be good to me.

decisions.choice: the wood offering
decisions.reason: The altar fire had to be kept burning always (Leviticus 6:5-6). The people had pledged to bring wood for it by lots, family by family, at set times (10:35), and to bring the firstfruits (10:36).

decisions.choice: Remember me, my God, for good: the book's last words
decisions.reason: The book ends with Nehemiah's prayer, as in 5:19 and 13:14, 22: he asks God to remember his work and treat him with favor. The word "good" here means God's kindness toward him.

decisions.choice: Remember for me, my God, for good (Literal); Remember me, my God, for good (Balanced); My God, remember me and be good to me (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of Nehemiah's prayer set for the whole book (5:19; 13:14, 22).

decisions.choice: I provided; I also arranged
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the list from verse 30 without a verb; Balanced and Readable supply one.
